Week 4 Edition • October 06, 2026

McMillan goes ballistic, Honk Dawgs earn an asterisk, and lexxyfour finally wins

WEEK 4  •  Kings of New York won by 67.4  •  lexxyfour broke the drought with 157.5  •  Honk Dawgs stand alone at 4–0
This WeekStandingsNumbersGame StoriesAwardsPower RankingsTrades
October 06, 2026 • Source: Sleeper API • Week 4 final

Week 4 had all the suspense of a lawn mower running over six fantasy lineups: the smallest margin was 36.8 points. Tetairoa McMillan detonated for 38.2, lexxyfour kicked down the winless-basement door with a league-leading 157.5, and every matchup finished as a full-body chalk outline. Honk Dawgs are the lone 4–0 team, though a schedule built from folding chairs has officially put that crown under investigation. Meanwhile, three mid-week trades shuffled enough firepower to make half the league check its receipts and the other half pretend they “liked the long-term value.”

Game Stories

Every matchup gets the front-page treatment

BLOWOUT

MCMILLAN GOES NUCLEAR; KINGS SEND A 67-POINT RANSOM NOTE

Kings of New York def. Everybody Hurts | 156.8 – 89.4

Tetairoa McMillan delivered the week’s best individual score and a season high for a wide receiver: 38.2. Rookie Kyle Monangai piled on 27.5, and the pair’s 65.7 outscored one entire Big Ballers roster. Two players beat a full starting lineup. That is not a stat; that is a public humiliation with decimals.

Sam LaPorta added 18.4, Derrick Henry 14.9 and Brenton Strange 13.0. Everybody Hurts got 22.2 from Jonathan Taylor and 15.0 from George Kittle, then drove directly off the cliff: Jeremiyah Love scored 6.0 and Emeka Egbuka 2.3. The 67.4-point margin broke the previous league mark of 64.6 from Week 1 and left the record book asking for hazard pay.

“We asked them to stop at 120. Apparently our email went to spam.” — Everybody Hurts

UPSET

LEXXYFOUR FINDS THE WIN COLUMN, IMMEDIATELY PARKS 157 IN IT

lexxyfour def. Steven diggs | 157.5 – 111.1

Kyren Williams went for 31.7, Kenneth Walker announced his Kansas City chapter with 30.4, Romeo Doubs added 20.8 and Carnell Tate 17.0. That is how an 0–3 team posts the week’s top score and the second-highest total of the season — even with Ja’Marr Chase limited to 4.2 after a concussion. The drought did not end politely; it left tire marks on Steven diggs.

Drake Maye’s 27.2 sat on lexxyfour’s bench behind Sam Darnold’s 14.3, but the lineup survived its own clown car. Steven diggs scored a respectable 111.1 behind Chuba Hubbard’s 25.4 and a 21.8-point debut from Zay Flowers. Lamar Jackson added 18.9 and Jaylen Warren 14.1, while DJ Moore’s shoulder flared again on a 2.2-point day. The injuries are real; the fantasy consequence was a perfectly decent score getting fed into a wood chipper.

“I benched 27 points and still won by 46. Please submit all coaching complaints in the trash can.” — lexxyfour

DRAMA

AOOOOK UNPACKS THE NEW TOYS; LOTES KEEPS THE RECEIPT AND THE LOSS

Pirates of the CaribBijan def. lotes | 151.5 – 112.2

Nico Collins scored 27.3, Bijan Robinson 27.2, C.J. Stroud 23.1 and T.J. Hockenson 18.4. Then the Oct. 1 imports checked in: Jameson Williams scored 13.2, Jaxon Smith-Njigba 10.1 and, from the next day’s deal, Bhayshul Tuten 10.1. The overhaul produced an immediate 151.5-point win and the kind of victory lap that makes a group chat mysteriously quiet.

lotes got the revenge-game package. CeeDee Lamb scored 32.8 four days after Steven diggs traded him away, and Devaughn Vele added 14.4; the two ex-Darren players combined for 47.2. Quinshon Judkins chipped in 18.6. But new arrival Jaylen Wright scored 0.7, which is less a debut than a typo, and the scoreboard declined to award points for narrative symmetry.

“We won the trade emotionally. Sadly, the league still uses points.” — lotes

COMEDY

J9 MAKES A ROSTER MOVE; POINTS FILE A RESTRAINING ORDER

Mommas Home <3 def. @J9 made a roster move. | 141.7 – 81.7

Javonte Williams led with 28.8, Puka Nacua returned for 23.2, and Ashton Jeanty, Deebo Samuel and Aaron Jones all landed between 14.8 and 15.6. Mommas Home did not need a miracle; it needed J9 to keep being J9, which remains the league’s most bankable game plan.

Jared Goff’s 20.5 was the lone bright spot. Chase Brown managed 13.6, then the trapdoor opened: Davante Adams 5.2, Chig Okonkwo 1.5 and newly added Isaiah Davis 0.0. Last week, this team won with 97.9. This week it scored 81.7 and lost by 60. J9 did not beat the allegations; he laminated them.

“We made a roster move. The roster asked us to put it back.” — @J9 made a roster move.

GAME RECAP

RICE CLOCKS IN, SCORES ZERO, LEAVES CMC MACHINE ON CINDER BLOCKS

Romo’s Rum Runner def. The CMC Machine | 123.1 – 86.3

Tee Higgins led Romo’s Rum Runner with 21.2. Josh Allen added 19.5, Rhamondre Stevenson 16.9, Jahmyr Gibbs 15.7 and Tucker Kraft 13.5. Balanced, clean, and completely unnecessary to dramatize — like winning a fistfight against a coat rack.

The CMC Machine got 20.2 from Malik Nabers, 18.1 from Dak Prescott and 14.5 from Christian McCaffrey. Then three starters combined for 2.5: Rashee Rice scored 0.0, Courtland Sutton 0.9 and Kalif Raymond 1.6. Two starting receivers totaled less than one point. This was not a machine; it was three loose screws in a trench coat.

“The check-engine light has been on since warmups. We simply chose faith.” — The CMC Machine

BLOWOUT

HONK DAWGS REACH 4–0 BY TRIPPING OVER ANOTHER SPEED BUMP

Honk Dawgs def. I WILL FUCK MADISON BEER | 111.3 – 56.5

Brock Bowers scored 17.6, Patrick Mahomes 17.0, Chris Olave 15.6 and James Cook 15.3. Honk Dawgs barely broke a sweat, barely broke 111, and still became the league’s last unbeaten team. Joe Burrow’s 25.7 stayed on the bench like a sports car in a driveway where the lawn mower already won the race.

Tyler Shough’s 15.9 was the losing side’s team high. Saquon Barkley scored 1.5, Ladd McConkey 0.0, Dalton Kincaid 1.2 and Jauan Jennings 1.3. The 56.5 total was the second-lowest score of the season and less than lexxyfour’s two starting running backs combined. Saquon arrived with a bib, a binky and exactly one-and-a-half points.

“We had a game plan. Then the game filed a missing-person report.” — I WILL FUCK MADISON BEER

Fraud Watch

Case file • undefeated, untested, under investigation

Honk Dawgs

Record: 4–0  •  This week: 111.3  •  Opponents’ record: 5–11

The crown is real. The road to it was made of traffic cones. Honk Dawgs beat lexxyfour 107.8–94.8, Romo’s Rum Runner 139.2–110.0, Steven diggs 118.4–69.0 and I WILL FUCK MADISON BEER 111.3–56.5. Three of four opponents failed to crack 100. The best team he has beaten scored 110.

His own season high is 139.2 — he has not touched 140 once. The last two opponents combined for 125.5 points across two full weeks, which is less competition than a bye with paperwork. Four wins, zero quality opponents, one crown from the party-supply aisle.

Verdict: 4–0 against traffic cones. Wake the Desk when he beats someone with a pulse.

Weekly Awards

Tony Snell Windsprint Award

Rashee Rice • 0.0

The starter who did absolutely nothing, named for Tony Snell’s immortal 28-minute zero-stat game. Rice matched the spirit perfectly: no points, no fingerprints, possibly never in the building.

Nick Foles Award

The backup who could have won it all — except lexxyfour won by 46 anyway. Sam Darnold’s 14.3 started in his place.

Joe Burrow Award

CeeDee Lamb • 32.8

Best performance in a loss. Four days after Steven diggs traded him away, Lamb delivered the revenge line and still lost by 39.3.
